sources.note: Mboa is 'apparently extinct' (citing Blench 2011); the Jarawan page's bibliography names Strümpell 1910 as the Mboa wordlist and adds 'Mohammadou (1980) contains a wordlist for Mboa, also called Mbɔŋa', summarized in Mohammadou 2002/2020. No phonological information.

sources.citation: Green, Christopher R. 2022. The mistaken identity of the Jarawa who traveled north: toward a re-classification of 'Jarawan Bantu'. Talk abstract, ICU-LINC African linguistics talk series, International Christian University (Tokyo), 5 February 2022 (online).
sources.note: Nothing on tone, stress or accent; the abstract argues ~20% cognacy with Proto-Bantu shared equally with Proto-Grassfields/Proto-Benue-Congo, Grassfields-like morphology, and absence of the NW-Bantu *k > zero, *g > k innovations, hence Jarawan as non-Bantu Bantoid.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger M. 2006. Jarawan Bantu: New Data and its Relation to Bantu. MS, 20 pp.
sources.note: The only modern synthesis that treats the Cameroon Jarawan languages (Mboa, Nagumi) together with the Nigerian ones and reviews all sources; may carry a phonological note on tone/accent, and lists whatever later Mboa data exist.

sources.note: Nothing. The article treats perfective and habitual/future verbal extensions in Jaar and Mbula, with stem-weight-conditioned allomorphy (-m/-Vm/-ma); no statement about tone, stress or accent in any Jarawan language, and explicitly no data on the Cameroonian languages (Mboa, Nagumi). scanned text saved alongside;scan has no text); the scanned string 'Heavy stress' on p. 6 is a misread of 'Heavy stems'.

sources.citation: Strümpell, F. 1910. Vergleichendes Wörterverzeichnis der Heidensprachen Adamauas. Mit Vorbemerkungen von Bernhard Struck. Zeitschrift für Ethnologie 42: 444-488.
sources.note: Comparative wordlist of 29 Adamawa languages; Mboa is column/row 28 'Mboa (östl. Kongola)'. Struck's Vorbemerkungen (p. 447) say only that the accent mark in the lists in many cases marks the musical high or higher-mid tone ('Der Akzent bezeichnet in vielen Fällen.. den musikalischen Hoch- oder höheren Mittelton'); p. 452 note calls Mboa an isolated language remnant with Bantu loans. Nothing on word stress. Rotated wordlist table scanned is garbled.
